     5→## Project Overview
     6→
     7→This is an ESP32-S3-LCD-2 development repository for creating OAISYS25 conference badge firmware. The project focuses on optimized video playback and hardware interfacing with the Waveshare ESP32-S3-LCD-2 development board.
     8→
     9→## Hardware Target
    10→
    11→**ESP32-S3-LCD-2 Board:**
    12→- 240x320 ST7789 LCD display (SPI)
    13→- QMI8658 IMU sensor (I2C)
    14→- Camera support
    15→- SD card slot
    16→- 16MB Flash with FFat partition layout
    17→
    18→**Key Pins:**
    19→- LCD: CS=45, DC=42, BL=1, SCK=39, MOSI=38, MISO=40
    20→- SPI shared with SD card and LCD
    21→- I2C: SCL=47, SDA=48 (IMU and Touch Panel)
    22→- Serial: TXD=43, RXD=44
    23→- USB: D-=19, D+=20 (occupied, not available for GPIO)

    55→- Incorrect structure will cause "Sketch not found" errors
    56→
    57→**Build and Upload:**
    58→```bash
    59→# Use Arduino IDE 2.x or arduino-cli

    62→# PSRAM: OPI PSRAM
    63→```
    64→
    65→**Upload Data to FFat Partition:**

    70→
    71→This script:
    72→1. Packages `data/` folder using mkfatfs
    73→2. Flashes to FFat partition at offset 0x611000 (0x610000 + 0x1000)
    74→3. Requires `esptool.py` and `mkfatfs` tools

    76→**Serial Monitor:**
    77→```bash
    78→# Most sketches use 115200 baud

    89→## Code Architecture
    90→
    91→### Video Player Architecture (`working_protos/video_loop`)
    92→
    93→This is the primary working prototype - heavily optimized from 250+ lines to 103 lines.
    94→
    95→**Design Pattern:**
    96→- **MemoryStream class**: Minimal Stream implementation for PSRAM buffer access
    97→- **VideoPlayer class**: Encapsulates display, flash I/O, and MJPEG decoding
    98→- **Singleton pattern**: Static instance for JPEG callback access
    99→- **RAII initialization**: All setup in `begin()`, simple `play()` for loop
   100→
   101→**Workflow:**
   102→1. `setup()`: Call `player.begin()` - initializes display, mounts FFat, loads `/output.mjpeg` to PSRAM
   103→2. `loop()`: Call `player.play()` - decodes next frame, auto-loops on EOF
   104→
   105→**Memory Management:**
   106→- Video loaded to PSRAM via `ps_malloc()` at startup
   107→- Decode buffer in heap: `320 * 240 / 2` bytes
   108→- No reloading during playback - pure memory streaming
   109→
   110→### Factory Demo Architecture (`ESP32-S3-LCD-2-Demo/Arduino/examples/01_factory`)
   111→
   112→Multi-module reference implementation showing full hardware capabilities.
   113→
   114→**BSP Layer (Board Support Package):**
   115→- `bsp_spi.h/.cpp`: Shared SPI bus with semaphore protection
   116→- `bsp_i2c.h/.cpp`: I2C bus for IMU
   117→- `bsp_lv_port.h/.cpp`: LVGL display driver integration
   118→- `bsp_button.h/.cpp`: Hardware button handling
   119→
   120→**App Layer:**
   121→- `app_qmi8658`: IMU data reading and visualization
   122→- `app_system`: System monitoring (battery, brightness)
   123→- `app_camera`: Camera integration
   124→- `app_wifi`: WiFi scanning and connection
   125→
   126→**UI Layer:**
   127→- `lvgl_ui/`: LVGL tabview UI
   128→- Each tab corresponds to an app module
   129→
   130→**Initialization Sequence:**
   131→```cpp
   132→setup() {
   133→  bsp_i2c_init();      // I2C bus
   134→  bsp_lv_port_init();  // Display + LVGL
   135→  bsp_spi_init();      // Shared SPI
   136→  bsp_button_init();   // Buttons
   137→
   138→  lvgl_ui_init();      // UI components
   139→
   140→  app_*_init();        // Module initialization
   141→  app_*_run();         // Start module tasks
   142→}
   143→```
   144→
   145→### Key Libraries
   146→
   147→**Arduino_GFX_Library:**
   148→- Hardware abstraction for ST7789 display
   149→- SPI bus configuration: `Arduino_ESP32SPI`
   150→- Display driver: `Arduino_ST7789` (240x320, IPS mode)
   151→
   152→**LVGL (Light and Versatile Graphics Library):**
   153→- Must configure `lv_conf.h` before use
   154→- Factory example uses LVGL 8.x API
   155→- Thread safety via `lvgl_lock()`/`lvgl_unlock()`
   156→
   157→**JPEGDEC:**
   158→- Software JPEG decoder
   159→- Used by MjpegClass for frame-by-frame decoding
   160→- Callback-based rendering: `JPEG_DRAW_CALLBACK`
   161→
   162→**MjpegClass:**
   163→- Custom MJPEG container parser (not a library)
   164→- Searches for JPEG markers (0xFFD8/0xFFD9) in stream
   165→- Extracts individual frames for JPEGDEC
   166→
   167→## FFat Partition Layout
   168→
   169→From `app3M_fat9M_16MB.csv`:
   170→```
   171→# Name,   Type, SubType, Offset,  Size
   172→nvs,      data, nvs,     0x9000,  0x5000
   173→otadata,  data, ota,     0xe000,  0x2000
   174→app0,     app,  ota_0,   0x10000, 0x300000
   175→app1,     app,  ota_1,   0x310000,0x300000
   176→ffat,     data, fat,     0x610000,0x9E0000
   177→```
   178→
   179→**Important:** Flash FFat images at offset **0x611000** (+0x1000 from partition start)
   180→
   181→## PSRAM Usage
   182→
   183→**Enabled via Arduino IDE settings:** OPI PSRAM
   184→
   185→**Allocation:**
   186→```cpp
   187→uint8_t* buffer = (uint8_t*)ps_malloc(size);  // PSRAM
   188→uint8_t* buffer = (uint8_t*)malloc(size);     // Heap
   189→```
   190→
   191→**Best Practice:**
   192→- Large buffers (>100KB): Use PSRAM
   193→- Frame buffers, video data: PSRAM
   194→- Small work buffers: Heap
   195→
   196→## Common Patterns
   197→
   198→### SPI Bus Sharing
   199→
   200→Multiple devices (LCD, SD card) share SPI bus - must use semaphore:
   201→
   202→```cpp
   203→if (bsp_spi_lock(-1)) {
   204→  // SPI operations
   205→  bsp_spi_unlock();
   206→}
   207→```
   208→
   209→### LVGL Thread Safety
   210→
   211→All LVGL calls must be protected:
   212→
   213→```cpp
   214→if (lvgl_lock(-1)) {
   215→  // LVGL UI updates
   216→  lvgl_unlock();
   217→}
   218→```
   219→
   220→### Stream-based File I/O
   221→
   222→Prefer Stream abstraction for memory/file interchangeability:
   223→
   224→```cpp
   225→class MemoryStream : public Stream {
   226→  // Implement available(), read(), peek(), readBytes()
   227→};
   228→```
   229→
   230→## Optimization Philosophy
   231→
   232→The `video_loop` prototype demonstrates aggressive optimization:
   233→
   234→**Removed:**
   235→- All Serial.print() debug output
   236→- Verbose error screens
   237→- Statistics tracking
   238→- Redundant comments and temporary variables
   239→
   240→**Retained:**
   241→- All functionality
   242→- Error detection (via return values)
   243→- Minimal LED feedback for critical failures
   244→
   245→**Result:** 59% code reduction (250→103 lines) with zero performance impact
   246→
   247→When modifying code, prioritize:
   248→1. Encapsulation over globals
   249→2. Classes over procedural code
   250→3. Minimal interfaces (begin/run pattern)
   251→4. Fail-fast error handling
   252→5. Production code = no debug spam
   253→
   254→## GPIO Pin Availability
   255→
   256→Based on ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-2 schematic **PinOut** section:
   257→
   258→**Pins broken out to headers:**
   259→- IO2, IO4, IO6-18, IO21, IO43, IO44, IO47, IO48
   260→
   261→**Truly free pins** (no peripherals attached):
   262→- **GPIO 18** - Completely free
   263→- **GPIO 2, 4, 6-17, 21** - Camera pins (safe if camera not attached)
   264→
   265→**Occupied pins:**
   266→- GPIO 0 (BOOT), 1 (BL), 5 (BAT) - System
   267→- GPIO 19, 20 - USB D-, D+ (**not available**)
   268→- GPIO 33-37 - **NOT broken out** to headers
   269→- GPIO 38-42, 45 - SPI (LCD/SD card)
   270→- GPIO 43, 44 - Serial console (U0_TXD/RXD)
   271→- GPIO 46 - Touch panel interrupt
   272→- GPIO 47, 48 - I2C (IMU and touch panel)
   273→
   274→## Audio Hardware
   275→
   276→### Microphone (INMP441)
   277→- **Pins:** GPIO 2 (BCK), 4 (WS), 18 (DIN)
   278→- **I2S Port:** I2S_NUM_0 (RX mode)
   279→- **Config:** Stereo capable, 24-bit samples, 16kHz sample rate
   280→- **Test sketch:** `workbench/mic_pin_test/` or `workbench/single_mic_test/`
   281→
   282→### Speaker (MAX98357A)
   283→- **Pins:** GPIO 6 (BCLK), 7 (LRC), 8 (DIN)
   284→- **I2S Port:** I2S_NUM_1 (TX mode)
   285→- **Power:** 5V recommended for full power (3-5W capable)
   286→- **Config:** 16-bit samples, 44.1kHz sample rate, mono/stereo
   287→- **Test sketch:** `workbench/speaker_test/`
   288→- **Note:** GAIN pin controls volume (Float=9dB, GND=12dB, VDD=15dB)
   289→

     1→# microWakeWord Training Notebook
     2→
     3→Train custom wake word models compatible with ESP32-S3 using the microWakeWord framework.
     4→
     5→## Overview
     6→
     7→This notebook trains models that work with `wakeword_pretrained_test.ino`:
     8→- **Input**: 40-bin log-mel spectrogram (30ms window, 10ms stride)
     9→- **Architecture**: MixNet streaming model
    10→- **Output**: Quantized int8 TFLite model
    11→
    12→## Training Approach
    13→
    14→Based on [microWakeWord](https://github.com/kahrendt/microWakeWord):
    15→
    16→1. **Synthetic sample generation** - Piper TTS creates diverse voice samples
    17→2. **Data augmentation** - Background noise, reverb, pitch shift, EQ
    18→3. **Negative sampling** - Speech and noise datasets prevent false accepts
    19→4. **Streaming conversion** - Model runs frame-by-frame on ESP32
    20→
    21→## Quick Start
    22→
    23→1. Open `wakeword_training.ipynb` in Google Colab
    24→2. Wake word is pre-configured as "Hey Daisy" in Cell 4:
    25→   ```python
    26→   WAKE_WORD = "Hey Daisy"
    27→   PHONETIC_VARIATIONS = ["Hey Daisy", "hey daisy", "hey day zee", ...]
    28→   ```
    29→3. Run all cells (~30-60 minutes with GPU)
    30→4. Download `hey_daisy.tflite`
    31→5. Copy to SD card at `/models/`
    32→
    33→## Requirements
    34→
    35→- Google Colab with GPU runtime (recommended)
    36→- ~5GB disk space for datasets
    37→- Internet connection for downloads
    38→
    39→## Output Files
    40→
    41→- `{wake_word}.tflite` - Quantized model for ESP32
    42→- `{wake_word}.json` - Model manifest with parameters
    43→
    44→## Deployment
    45→
    46→1. Copy `.tflite` to SD card: `/models/hey_daisy.tflite`

    56→
    57→## Tuning Tips
    58→
    59→| Issue | Solution |
    60→|-------|----------|
    61→| Too many false positives | Increase `PROBABILITY_CUTOFF` |
    62→| Too many false negatives | Decrease `PROBABILITY_CUTOFF` |
    63→| Inconsistent detection | Add phonetic variations, retrain |

    66→## Training Parameters

    70→| Parameter | Default | Description |

     1→# microWakeWord - Hey Daisy
     2→
     3→Wake word detection using custom trained microWakeWord TFLite model with EdgeNeuron library.
     4→
     5→**Wake word: "Hey Daisy"**
     6→
     7→## How It Works
     8→
     9→1. **Audio capture**: INMP441 microphone at 16kHz, 16-bit mono
    10→2. **Feature extraction**: Microfrontend generates 40-bin spectrogram features
    11→3. **Inference**: EdgeNeuron runs TFLite model every 10ms
    12→4. **Detection**: Sliding window averages probabilities, triggers at threshold
    13→
    14→## Setup
    15→
    16→### 1. Install Libraries
    17→
    18→**Required libraries** (via Arduino Library Manager):
    19→- **EdgeNeuron** by Consentium IoT
    20→- **ArduinoJson** by Benoit Blanchon
    21→
    22→### 2. Copy Files to SD Card
    23→
    24→```
    25→SD Card/
    26→└── models/
    27→    ├── hey_daisy.tflite    # The trained model
    28→    └── hey_daisy.json      # Configuration manifest
    29→```
    30→
    31→### 3. JSON Configuration
    32→
    33→The `hey_daisy.json` file controls tunable detection parameters:
    34→
    35→```json
    36→{
    37→  "type": "micro",
    38→  "wake_word": "Hey Daisy",
    39→  "model": "hey_daisy.tflite",
    40→  "version": 1,
    41→  "micro": {
    42→    "probability_cutoff": 0.5,
    43→    "sliding_window_average_size": 10,
    44→    "min_high_frames": 6,
    45→    "min_frame_prob": 0.5,
    46→    "cooldown_ms": 1500
    47→  }
    48→}
    49→```
    50→
    51→**Parameters:**
    52→| Parameter | Description | Default |
    53→|-----------|-------------|---------|
    54→| `probability_cutoff` | Average probability threshold to trigger | 0.5 |
    55→| `sliding_window_average_size` | Number of frames to average | 10 |
    56→| `min_high_frames` | Minimum frames above `min_frame_prob` | 6 |
    57→| `min_frame_prob` | Per-frame probability threshold | 0.5 |
    58→| `cooldown_ms` | Milliseconds to ignore after detection | 1500 |
    59→
    60→### 4. Board Settings
    61→
    62→- Board: ESP32S3 Dev Module
    63→- PSRAM: OPI PSRAM
    64→- Flash Size: 16MB
    65→
    66→### 5. Upload and Test
    67→
    68→1. Insert SD card with model and config
    69→2. Upload sketch
    70→3. Open Serial Monitor (115200 baud)
    71→4. Say "Hey Daisy" - LED lights up on detection
    72→
    73→## Expected Output
    74→
    75→```
    76→=== microWakeWord - Hey Daisy ===
    77→
    78→SD Card: OK
    79→Config loaded: /models/hey_daisy.json
    80→
    81→Configuration:
    82→  Wake word: "Hey Daisy"
    83→  Probability cutoff: 0.50
    84→  Sliding window size: 10
    85→  Min high frames: 6
    86→  Min frame prob: 0.50
    87→  Cooldown: 1500 ms
    88→
    89→Model loaded: 132848 bytes
    90→TFLite: OK
    91→  Arena used: 89432 bytes
    92→  Input: dims=[1,3,40], type=9
    93→  Output: dims=[1,1], type=9
    94→Microphone: OK
    95→Frontend: OK
    96→
    97→Listening for "Hey Daisy"...
    98→================================
    99→
   100→prob: 0.012, avg: 0.008, high: 0/10
   101→prob: 0.867, avg: 0.512, high: 7/10
   102→prob: 0.994, avg: 0.871, high: 9/10
   103→
   104→>>> Hey Daisy DETECTED! <<<
   105→```
   106→
   107→## Tuning Tips
   108→
   109→**Too many false positives:**
   110→- Increase `probability_cutoff` (try 0.7, 0.8, 0.9)
   111→- Increase `min_high_frames` (try 8 or 10)
   112→- Increase `min_frame_prob` (try 0.6 or 0.7)
   113→
   114→**Missing detections:**
   115→- Decrease `probability_cutoff` (try 0.3 or 0.4)
   116→- Decrease `min_high_frames` (try 4 or 5)
   117→- Speak closer to microphone
   118→
   119→**Multiple triggers per wake word:**
   120→- Increase `cooldown_ms` (try 2000 or 2500)
   121→
   122→## Troubleshooting
   123→
   124→### "Cannot open config" / "Config load failed"
   125→- Check SD card has `/models/hey_daisy.json`
   126→- Verify JSON syntax is valid
   127→
   128→### "Model load failed"
   129→- Check SD card has `/models/hey_daisy.tflite`
   130→- Try reformatting SD card as FAT32
   131→
   132→### "TFLite init failed"
   133→- Model may need more memory - check serial for specific error
   134→- TENSOR_ARENA_SIZE is set to 500KB which should be sufficient

     1→# YAMNet-1024 Audio Embedding on ESP32-S3
     2→
     3→Extract 1024-dimensional audio embeddings using YAMNet on ESP32-S3 with dual-core optimization.
     4→
     5→## Overview
     6→
     7→This sketch:
     8→1. **Records 3-5 seconds** of audio from dual INMP441 microphones (downmixed to mono)
     9→2. **Generates mel-spectrogram** (64 mels × 96 frames) using ESP-DSP accelerated FFT
    10→3. **Runs YAMNet-1024 inference** with TensorFlow Lite Micro (dual-core optimized)
    11→4. **Extracts 1024-D embeddings** from the model
    12→5. **Saves to SD card** as JSON format
    13→
    14→## Hardware Requirements
    15→
    16→- **ESP32-S3-LCD-2** board (or any ESP32-S3 with PSRAM)
    17→- **2× INMP441** MEMS microphones (I2S)
    18→- **SD card** (FAT32 formatted, 4GB+ recommended)
    19→- **Micro SD card reader/writer** (for loading model file)
    20→
    21→## Arduino IDE Setup
    22→
    23→### 1. Install Arduino Libraries
    24→
    25→Open Arduino IDE → Tools → Manage Libraries, then install:
    26→
    27→**Required:**
    28→- `TensorFlowLite_ESP32` by Kazuhiro Tanaka
    29→- (ESP-DSP is included with ESP32 Arduino core)
    30→
    31→**Note:** ESP-DSP library is built into the ESP32 Arduino core (esp-dsp component).
    32→
    33→### 2. Board Configuration
    34→
    35→- **Board:** ESP32S3 Dev Module
    36→- **Partition Scheme:** 16MB Flash (3MB APP/9MB FATFS)
    37→- **PSRAM:** OPI PSRAM
    38→- **Upload Speed:** 921600
    39→- **Core Debug Level:** None (or Info for debugging)
    40→
    41→## Model Download and Setup
    42→
    43→### Download YAMNet TFLite Model
    44→
    45→**Official Source: Kaggle (Recommended)**
    46→
    47→1. Visit: https://www.kaggle.com/models/google/yamnet/tfLite/classification-tflite/1
    48→2. Click "Download" button (requires free Kaggle account)
    49→3. Download: `yamnet_classification.tflite` (approx. 3.5-4 MB)
    50→
    51→**Alternative: Convert from TensorFlow Hub**
    52→```python
    53→# Python script to convert YAMNet to TFLite
    54→import tensorflow_hub as hub
    55→import tensorflow as tf
    56→
    57→model = hub.load('https://tfhub.dev/google/yamnet/1')
    58→# ... conversion code (see Kaggle yamnet-tflite notebook)
    59→```
    60→
    61→**For STMicroelectronics YAMNet-256 (smaller, faster)**
    62→- GitHub: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32ai-modelzoo
    63→- Navigate to: `audio_event_detection/yamnet/ST_pretrainedmodel_public_dataset/`
    64→- Choose ESC-10 or FSD50K dataset folder
    65→- Download: `yamnet_256_64x96_tl_int8.tflite` (~167 KB)
    66→
    67→### Prepare SD Card
    68→
    69→1. Format SD card as **FAT32**
    70→2. Rename the downloaded model file to: `yamnet.tflite`
    71→   - From Kaggle: `yamnet_classification.tflite` → `yamnet.tflite`
    72→   - From STM32: `yamnet_256_64x96_tl_int8.tflite` → `yamnet.tflite`
    73→3. Copy `yamnet.tflite` to the **root directory** of SD card
    74→4. Insert SD card into ESP32-S3-LCD-2
    75→
    76→The SD card structure should look like:
    77→```
    78→SD:/
    79→├── yamnet.tflite        (model file, 167KB-4MB depending on version)
    80→└── embedding.json       (will be created by sketch)
    81→```
    82→
    83→## Wiring Diagram
    84→
    85→### INMP441 Microphones → ESP32-S3 (I2S0)
    86→
    87→```
    88→ESP32-S3-LCD-2          INMP441 #1 (LEFT)      INMP441 #2 (RIGHT)
    89→────────────────        ─────────────────      ──────────────────
    90→3.3V ───────────┬────── VDD                    VDD
    91→                │
    92→GND ────────────┼────── GND ──────────┬─────── GND
    93→                │                     │
    94→GPIO 2 (BCK) ───┼────── SCK ──────────┼─────── SCK
    95→GPIO 4 (WS) ────┼────── WS ───────────┼─────── WS
    96→GPIO 18 (DIN) ──┴────── SD ───────────┴─────── SD
    97→                        │                      │
    98→                        L/R → GND              L/R → 3.3V
    99→                          (LEFT)                 (RIGHT)
   100→```
   101→
   102→**Pin Summary:**
   103→| Function      | ESP32 Pin | Device Pin     |
   104→|---------------|-----------|----------------|
   105→| Bit Clock     | GPIO 2    | SCK (both mics)|
   106→| Word Select   | GPIO 4    | WS (both mics) |
   107→| Data In       | GPIO 18   | SD (both mics) |
   108→| Left Channel  | —         | Mic #1 L/R → GND |
   109→| Right Channel | —         | Mic #2 L/R → 3.3V |
   110→
   111→### SD Card (SPI)
   112→
   113→SD card uses the built-in SD slot on ESP32-S3-LCD-2:
   114→- **CS:** GPIO 41
   115→- **MOSI:** GPIO 38
   116→- **MISO:** GPIO 40
   117→- **SCK:** GPIO 39
   118→
   119→## Upload and Run
   120→
   121→1. Connect ESP32-S3-LCD-2 to computer via USB-C
   122→2. Open `yamnet_audio_embedding.ino` in Arduino IDE
   123→3. Select board and port
   124→4. Click **Upload**
   125→5. Open **Serial Monitor** at **115200 baud**

   198→
   199→## Configuration
   200→
   201→Edit these constants in `yamnet_audio_embedding.ino`:
   202→
   203→```cpp
   204→const int RECORD_SECONDS = 3;  // Change to 3, 4, or 5 seconds
   205→```
   206→
   207→## Output Format
   208→
   209→The sketch creates `/embedding.json` on the SD card:
   210→
   211→```json
   212→{
   213→  "dimension": 1024,
   214→  "embeddings": [
   215→    0.234567,
   216→    -0.123456,
   217→    0.567890,
   218→    ...
   219→    (1024 values total)
   220→  ]
   221→}
   222→```
   223→
   224→## Memory Usage
   225→
   226→**PSRAM Allocation:**
   227→- Audio buffer (3 sec @ 16kHz): ~96 KB
   228→- Mel-spectrogram (64×96): ~24 KB
   229→- Model weights: ~3.9 MB
   230→- Tensor arena: 400 KB
   231→- Embeddings: 4 KB
   232→- **Total: ~4.4 MB** (fits comfortably in 8 MB PSRAM)
   233→
   234→**Heap Usage:**
   235→- TFLite infrastructure: ~50 KB
   236→- ESP-DSP FFT buffers: ~10 KB
   237→
   238→## Performance
   239→
   240→**Typical timing on ESP32-S3 @ 240MHz:**
   241→- Recording (3 sec): ~3000 ms
   242→- Mel-spectrogram: ~500 ms
   243→- YAMNet-1024 inference: **6-10 seconds** (dual-core optimized)
   244→- JSON write: ~150 ms
   245→- **Total: ~10-14 seconds**
   246→
   247→The inference is the bottleneck. YAMNet-1024 has 3.2M parameters - impressive for a microcontroller!
   248→
   249→## Troubleshooting
   250→
   251→### "Failed to load model from SD"
   252→- Check SD card is inserted
   253→- Verify `yamnet1024.tflite` exists in root directory
   254→- Try reformatting SD card as FAT32
   255→- Check file size is ~3-4 MB
   256→
   257→### "AllocateTensors() failed"
   258→- Model is too large or incompatible
   259→- Try increasing `TENSOR_ARENA_SIZE` in `yamnet_inference.h`
   260→- Check PSRAM is enabled in Arduino IDE settings
   261→
   262→### "Invoke() failed"
   263→- Model operations not supported
   264→- Check Serial Monitor for TFLite error messages
   265→- May need to add more ops to resolver in `yamnet_inference.cpp`
   266→
   267→### Very slow inference (>20 seconds)
   268→- Check CPU frequency is 240MHz (Tools → CPU Frequency)
   269→- Verify PSRAM is enabled
   270→- Model may be using PSRAM instead of SRAM (expected for large models)
   271→
   272→### Recording is silent
   273→- Check INMP441 wiring (GPIO 2, 4, 18)
   274→- Verify L/R pins: Mic #1 → GND, Mic #2 → 3.3V
   275→- Test with speaker_beep_test or dual_mic_sd_record
   276→
   277→### "Input tensor shape mismatch"
   278→- YAMNet expects [1, 96, 64, 1] or [1, 64, 96, 1]
   279→- Check model variant and adjust mel-spectrogram transpose if needed
   280→
   281→## Using a Smaller Model
   282→
   283→If YAMNet-1024 is too slow, use **YAMNet-256** instead:
   284→
   285→1. Download YAMNet-256 from STMicroelectronics:
   286→   ```
   287→   https://huggingface.co/STMicroelectronics/yamnet
   288→   ```
   289→
   290→2. Save as `yamnet256.tflite` on SD card
   291→
   292→3. Edit `yamnet_audio_embedding.ino`:
   293→   ```cpp
   294→   const char* MODEL_PATH = "/yamnet256.tflite";
   295→   ```
   296→
   297→4. Edit `yamnet_inference.h`:
   298→   ```cpp
   299→   #define EMBEDDING_DIM 256    // Change from 1024 to 256
   300→   ```
   301→
   302→YAMNet-256 is ~167 KB (fits in SRAM) and runs much faster (~1-2 seconds inference).
   303→
   304→## Technical Details
   305→
   306→### Mel-Spectrogram Preprocessing
   307→
   308→- **FFT size:** 512 (25ms window @ 16kHz)
   309→- **Hop length:** 160 samples (10ms)
   310→- **Mel bins:** 64
   311→- **Frames:** 96
   312→- **Frequency range:** 125-7500 Hz
   313→- **Window:** Hann window
   314→- **Transform:** Log mel-filterbank energies
   315→
   316→Preprocessing uses ESP-DSP's hardware-accelerated FFT for fast computation.
   317→
   318→### Dual-Core Optimization
   319→
   320→- **Core 0:** Main sketch, audio recording, mel-spectrogram
   321→- **Core 1:** TensorFlow Lite inference task
   322→
   323→This parallelization allows preprocessing to run concurrently with inference (though inference is still the bottleneck).
   324→
   325→### Model Architecture
   326→
   327→YAMNet-1024 uses MobileNetV1 architecture with depthwise-separable convolutions. The embedding layer (1024-D) sits before the final classification layer, capturing rich audio features.
   328→
   329→## Next Steps
   330→
   331→Once you have embeddings:
   332→
   333→1. **Audio similarity:** Compute cosine similarity between embeddings
   334→2. **Clustering:** Use k-means to group similar audio samples
   335→3. **Classification:** Train a simple classifier on top of embeddings
   336→4. **Voice identification:** Compare voice embeddings for speaker recognition
   337→5. **Anomaly detection:** Detect unusual sounds by embedding distance
   338→
   339→## References
   340→
   341→- [YAMNet Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.07850)
   342→- [TensorFlow Lite Micro](https://www.tensorflow.org/lite/microcontrollers)
   343→- [ESP-DSP Library](https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-dsp/)
   344→- [STMicroelectronics YAMNet](https://huggingface.co/STMicroelectronics/yamnet)

     5→This sketch demonstrates a complete audio capture and playback pipeline:
     6→1. **Records 30 seconds** of stereo audio from dual INMP441 microphones
     7→2. **Downmixes to mono** using HYBRID algorithm (adaptive + width)

    39→```
    40→MAX98357A               ESP32-S3-LCD-2
    41→─────────────           ────────────────
    42→VIN    ─────────────────→ 5V (or 3.3V)
    43→GND    ─────────────────→ GND
    44→BCLK   ─────────────────→ GPIO 6
    45→LRC    ─────────────────→ GPIO 7
    46→DIN    ─────────────────→ GPIO 8
    47→GAIN   ─────────────────→ Float (9dB) / GND (12dB) / VDD (15dB)
    48→SD     ─────────────────→ VIN (always on)
    49→
    50→SPK+   ─────────────────→ Speaker +
    51→SPK-   ─────────────────→ Speaker -
    52→```
    53→
    54→## Pin Summary
    55→
    56→| Function      | ESP32 Pin | Device Pin     | Notes                          |
    57→|---------------|-----------|----------------|--------------------------------|
    58→| **Microphones (I2S0)** |           |                |                                |
    59→| Bit Clock     | GPIO 2    | SCK (both mics)| Shared I2S bus                 |
    60→| Word Select   | GPIO 4    | WS (both mics) | Shared I2S bus                 |
    61→| Data In       | GPIO 18   | SD (both mics) | Shared I2S bus                 |
    62→| Left Channel  | —         | Mic #1 L/R → GND | Channel select                 |
    63→| Right Channel | —         | Mic #2 L/R → 3.3V | Channel select                 |
    64→| **Speaker (I2S1)** |           |                |                                |
    65→| Bit Clock     | GPIO 6    | BCLK           | Camera pin (safe if no camera) |
    66→| Word Select   | GPIO 7    | LRC            | Camera pin (safe if no camera) |
    67→| Data Out      | GPIO 8    | DIN            | Camera pin (safe if no camera) |
    68→| Power         | 5V        | VIN            | 3.3V also works (lower volume) |
    69→
    70→**Important:** GPIO 6, 7, 8 are camera pins from the schematic, but safe to use when the camera is not attached.
    71→
    72→## Audio Specifications
    73→
    74→| Parameter       | Value              |
    75→|-----------------|--------------------|
    76→| Sample Rate     | 16,000 Hz          |
    77→| Bit Depth       | 16-bit PCM         |
    78→| Recording       | 30 seconds stereo  |
    79→| Playback        | Mono (looped)      |
    80→| Downmix Method  | HYBRID (adaptive + width) |
    81→| Memory Usage    | ~1.92 MB PSRAM     |
    82→
    83→## Downmix Algorithm: HYBRID
    84→
    85→The HYBRID downmix algorithm combines the best of two approaches:
    86→
    87→- **Adaptive weighting**: Favors the microphone with stronger signal (clarity)
    88→- **30%-70% constraint**: Ensures both channels always contribute (width)
    89→
    90→This prevents the "interruption" feeling when blocking one mic while maintaining clarity and reducing background noise compared to simple averaging.
    91→
    92→## Usage Instructions
    93→
    94→### 1. Wire Everything
    95→
    96→Follow the wiring diagrams above. Critical points:
    97→
    98→- **Microphones**: Both share I2S bus (GPIO 2, 4, 18)
    99→  - Mic #1: L/R → **GND** (left channel)
   100→  - Mic #2: L/R → **3.3V** (right channel)
   101→
   102→- **Speaker**: Connect to I2S1 (GPIO 6, 7, 8)
   103→  - Use **5V** for full power (3.3V works but quieter)
   104→  - Connect speaker to SPK+ and SPK-
   105→  - Set GAIN pin for desired volume
   106→
   107→### 2. Upload the Sketch
   108→
   109→1. Open `record_play_loop.ino` in Arduino IDE
   110→2. Select **Board**: ESP32S3 Dev Module
   111→3. Select **Partition Scheme**: 16MB Flash (3MB APP/9MB FATFS)
   112→4. Select **PSRAM**: OPI PSRAM
   113→5. Upload
   114→
   115→### 3. Monitor Operation
   116→
   117→Open Serial Monitor at **115200 baud**:
   118→
   119→```
   120→========================================
   121→Record -> Downmix -> Playback Loop
   122→========================================
   123→
   124→Total PSRAM: 8388608 bytes
   125→Free PSRAM: 8257536 bytes
   126→
   127→Allocating stereo buffer (1920000 bytes)... OK
   128→Allocating mono buffer (960000 bytes)... OK
   129→
   130→Initializing I2S0 (microphones)... OK
   131→Initializing I2S1 (speaker)... OK
   132→
   133→Recording 30 seconds (stereo)...
   134→
   135→Progress: 10% (192000 / 960000 samples)
   136→Progress: 20% (384000 / 960000 samples)
   137→...
   138→Progress: 100% (960000 / 960000 samples)
   139→
   140→Recorded: 960000 samples in 30012 ms
   141→
   142→========================================
   143→Recording complete!
   144→========================================
   145→
   146→Applying HYBRID downmix... OK
   147→
   148→========================================
   149→Starting playback loop...
   150→========================================
   151→
   152→Playing... sample 0 / 480000
   153→Playing... sample 32768 / 480000
   154→...
   155→Playback complete, looping...
   156→```
   157→
   158→### 4. LED Feedback
   159→
   160→- **Blinking**: Recording in progress
   161→- **Solid ON**: Playback running
   162→
   163→## Testing Tips
   164→
   165→### Test Recording Quality
   166→
   167→During the 30-second recording:
   168→- Speak clearly from different positions
   169→- Tap near each microphone to verify both are working
   170→- Try speaking while moving between mics
   171→
   172→### Test Playback Volume
   173→
   174→If playback is too quiet or too loud:
   175→
   176→**Hardware adjustments:**
   177→- **GAIN pin**: Float (9dB), GND (12dB), or VDD (15dB)
   178→- **Power**: 5V gives more power than 3.3V
   179→- **Speaker**: 4-ohm speakers are louder than 8-ohm
   180→
   181→**Code adjustments (if needed):**
   182→```cpp
   183→// In playMonoBuffer(), scale samples before writing:
   184→int16_t scaled = mono_buffer[i] * 2;  // 2x gain (may clip!)
   185→i2s_write(I2S_NUM_1, &scaled, ...);
   186→```
   187→
   188→### Test Downmix Quality
   189→
   190→The HYBRID algorithm should provide:
   191→- ✅ Clear, intelligible voice
   192→- ✅ Captures from multiple directions
   193→- ✅ No "interruption" when blocking one mic
   194→- ✅ Less background noise than simple average
   195→
   196→## Troubleshooting
   197→
   198→### No audio from speaker
   199→
   200→- Check MAX98357A wiring (especially BCLK, LRC, DIN)
   201→- Verify speaker is connected to SPK+/SPK-
   202→- Try connecting SD pin to VIN (enable amplifier)
   203→- Check Serial Monitor for I2S1 initialization errors
   204→
   205→### Distorted/clipped audio
   206→
   207→- Lower GAIN pin setting (try Float = 9dB)
   208→- Check speaker impedance (4-8 ohm required)
   209→- Verify 5V power is stable
   210→
   211→### Quiet playback
   212→
   213→- Increase GAIN pin setting (connect to VDD = 15dB)
   214→- Use 5V instead of 3.3V for VIN
   215→- Use 4-ohm speaker instead of 8-ohm
   216→- **Software gain**: Increase `GAIN_BOOST` to 6.0f or 8.0f (line 235 in .ino)
   217→- **Recording level**: Speak very loudly into mics during recording, position mics 5-10cm from mouth
   218→
   219→### Recording noise/static
   220→
   221→- Check microphone wiring (especially L/R pins)
   222→- Verify both mics are powered (3.3V to VDD)
   223→- Ensure solid I2S connections (GPIO 2, 4, 18)
   224→- Try different microphones if one is defective
   225→
   226→### Playback loops too fast/slow
   227→
   228→- Sample rate mismatch - ensure both I2S buses use 16kHz
   229→- Check `SAMPLE_RATE` constant is 16000
   230→
   231→## How It Works
   232→
   233→### 1. Dual I2S Buses
   234→
   235→ESP32-S3 has multiple I2S peripherals:
   236→- **I2S_NUM_0**: Microphones (RX mode)
   237→- **I2S_NUM_1**: Speaker (TX mode)
   238→
   239→These run independently and can operate simultaneously.
   240→
   241→### 2. Recording Phase
   242→
   243→```
   244→I2S0 (mics) → i2s_buffer (32-bit) → stereo_buffer (16-bit, PSRAM)
   245→```
   246→
   247→Captures 30 seconds of stereo audio (left + right interleaved).
   248→
   249→### 3. Downmix Phase
   250→
   251→```
   252→stereo_buffer → HYBRID algorithm → mono_buffer (PSRAM)
   253→```
   254→
   255→Applies adaptive weighting with 30%-70% constraints.
   256→
   257→### 4. Playback Phase
   258→
   259→```
   260→mono_buffer → I2S1 (speaker) → Loop forever
   261→```
   262→
   263→Continuously plays the mono recording.
   264→
   265→## Next Steps
   266→
   267→Once you've verified the basic loop works:
   268→
   269→1. **Add voice activity detection (VAD)** - Only record when voice detected
   270→2. **Implement push-to-talk** - Button to trigger recording
   271→3. **Add effects** - Reverb, echo, pitch shift
   272→4. **Stream to WiFi** - Send audio over network
   273→5. **Add compression** - OPUS codec for smaller files
   274→6. **Dual direction** - Record while playing (walkie-talkie mode)
   275→
   276→## Technical References
   277→
   278→- **ESP32-S3 I2S**: [ESP-IDF I2S Documentation](https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf/en/latest/esp32s3/api-reference/peripherals/i2s.html)
   279→- **INMP441 Datasheet**: Omnidirectional I2S MEMS Microphone
   280→- **MAX98357A Datasheet**: I2S Class D Amplifier
   281→- **Hybrid Downmix**: Adaptive weighting with minimum contribution per channel
   282→
   283→---
   284→
   285→**Power Tip:** For battery operation, use 3.3V for MAX98357A VIN to reduce current draw. Volume will be lower but adequate for close listening!
   286→

   240→## Common Patterns
   241→
   242→### Dual I2S Audio Architecture
   243→
   244→ESP32-S3 supports separate I2S buses for simultaneous input/output:
   245→
   246→```cpp
   247→// I2S0 for microphones (RX)
   248→i2s_config_t mic_config = {
   249→  .mode = I2S_MODE_MASTER | I2S_MODE_RX,
   250→  .sample_rate = 16000,
   251→  .bits_per_sample = I2S_BITS_PER_SAMPLE_32BIT,  // INMP441 sends 24-bit in 32-bit frame
   252→  .channel_format = I2S_CHANNEL_FMT_RIGHT_LEFT,
   253→  // ...
   254→};
   255→i2s_driver_install(I2S_NUM_0, &mic_config, 0, NULL);
   256→
   257→// I2S1 for speaker (TX)
   258→i2s_config_t spk_config = {
   259→  .mode = I2S_MODE_MASTER | I2S_MODE_TX,
   260→  .sample_rate = 16000,
   261→  .bits_per_sample = I2S_BITS_PER_SAMPLE_16BIT,
   262→  // ...
   263→};
   264→i2s_driver_install(I2S_NUM_1, &spk_config, 0, NULL);
   265→```
   266→
   267→See `workbench/working_protos/02_speaker_mic_combo/` for full duplex example.
   268→
   269→### SPI Bus Sharing
   270→
   271→Multiple devices (LCD, SD card) share SPI bus - must use semaphore:
   272→
   273→```cpp
   274→if (bsp_spi_lock(-1)) {
   275→  // SPI operations
```

    98→**Design Pattern:**

   110→
   111→Port of llama2.c for on-device text generation.

   113→**Files:**
   114→- `llm_core.cpp/h` - Transformer forward pass, attention, RoPE
   115→- `tokenizer.cpp/h` - BPE tokenizer (SentencePiece format)

   125→### Wake Word Detection (`tests/wakeword_pretrained_test/`)
   126→
   127→microWakeWord-based detection using EdgeNeuron TFLite runtime.
   128→
   129→**Pipeline:**
   130→1. INMP441 mic → 16kHz audio capture
   131→2. Microfrontend → 40-bin log-mel spectrogram (30ms window, 10ms stride)
   132→3. EdgeNeuron → TFLite inference every 10ms
   133→4. Sliding window → Probability averaging → Detection trigger

   141→

   143→
   144→YAMNet-based 1024-D audio embeddings on ESP32-S3.
   145→
   146→**Pipeline:**
   147→1. Dual INMP441 mics → stereo capture → mono downmix
   148→2. ESP-DSP accelerated FFT → 64-mel × 96-frame spectrogram
   149→3. TensorFlowLite_ESP32 → YAMNet inference (dual-core optimized)
   150→4. Extract 1024-D embedding → JSON output
   151→
   152→**Performance:** ~10-14 seconds total (inference is the bottleneck at 6-10s).

   154→### Factory Demo Architecture (`ESP32-S3-LCD-2-Demo/Arduino/examples/01_factory`)
   155→
   156→Multi-module reference implementation showing full hardware capabilities.
   157→
   158→**BSP Layer (Board Support Package):**
   159→- `bsp_spi.h/.cpp`: Shared SPI bus with semaphore protection
   160→- `bsp_i2c.h/.cpp`: I2C bus for IMU
   161→- `bsp_lv_port.h/.cpp`: LVGL display driver integration
   162→- `bsp_button.h/.cpp`: Hardware button handling
   163→
   164→**App Layer:**
   165→- `app_qmi8658`: IMU data reading and visualization
   166→- `app_system`: System monitoring (battery, brightness)
   167→- `app_camera`: Camera integration
   168→- `app_wifi`: WiFi scanning and connection
   169→
   170→**UI Layer:**
   171→- `lvgl_ui/`: LVGL tabview UI
   172→- Each tab corresponds to an app module
   173→
   174→**Initialization Sequence:**
   175→```cpp
   176→setup() {
   177→  bsp_i2c_init();      // I2C bus
   178→  bsp_lv_port_init();  // Display + LVGL
   179→  bsp_spi_init();      // Shared SPI
   180→  bsp_button_init();   // Buttons
   181→
   182→  lvgl_ui_init();      // UI components
   183→
   184→  app_*_init();        // Module initialization
   185→  app_*_run();         // Start module tasks
   186→}
   187→```
   188→
   189→### Key Libraries
   190→
   191→**Arduino_GFX_Library:**
   192→- Hardware abstraction for ST7789 display
   193→- SPI bus configuration: `Arduino_ESP32SPI`
   194→- Display driver: `Arduino_ST7789` (240x320, IPS mode)
   195→
   196→**LVGL (Light and Versatile Graphics Library):**
   197→- Must configure `lv_conf.h` before use
   198→- Factory example uses LVGL 8.x API
   199→- Thread safety via `lvgl_lock()`/`lvgl_unlock()`
   200→
   201→**JPEGDEC:**
   202→- Software JPEG decoder
   203→- Used by MjpegClass for frame-by-frame decoding
   204→- Callback-based rendering: `JPEG_DRAW_CALLBACK`
   205→
   206→**MjpegClass:**
   207→- Custom MJPEG container parser (not a library)
   208→- Searches for JPEG markers (0xFFD8/0xFFD9) in stream
   209→- Extracts individual frames for JPEGDEC
   210→
   211→## FFat Partition Layout
   212→
   213→From `app3M_fat9M_16MB.csv`:
   214→```
   215→# Name,   Type, SubType, Offset,  Size
   216→nvs,      data, nvs,     0x9000,  0x5000
   217→otadata,  data, ota,     0xe000,  0x2000
   218→app0,     app,  ota_0,   0x10000, 0x300000
   219→app1,     app,  ota_1,   0x310000,0x300000
   220→ffat,     data, fat,     0x610000,0x9E0000
   221→```
   222→
   223→**Important:** Flash FFat images at offset **0x611000** (+0x1000 from partition start)
   224→
   225→## PSRAM Usage
   226→
   227→**Enabled via Arduino IDE settings:** OPI PSRAM
   228→
   229→**Allocation:**
   230→```cpp
   231→uint8_t* buffer = (uint8_t*)ps_malloc(size);  // PSRAM
   232→uint8_t* buffer = (uint8_t*)malloc(size);     // Heap
   233→```
   234→
   235→**Best Practice:**
   236→- Large buffers (>100KB): Use PSRAM
   237→- Frame buffers, video data: PSRAM
   238→- Small work buffers: Heap
   239→
   240→## Common Patterns
   241→
   242→### Dual I2S Audio Architecture
   243→
   244→ESP32-S3 supports separate I2S buses for simultaneous input/output:
   245→
   246→```cpp
   247→// I2S0 for microphones (RX)
   248→i2s_config_t mic_config = {
   249→  .mode = I2S_MODE_MASTER | I2S_MODE_RX,
   250→  .sample_rate = 16000,
   251→  .bits_per_sample = I2S_BITS_PER_SAMPLE_32BIT,  // INMP441 sends 24-bit in 32-bit frame
   252→  .channel_format = I2S_CHANNEL_FMT_RIGHT_LEFT,
   253→  // ...
   254→};
   255→i2s_driver_install(I2S_NUM_0, &mic_config, 0, NULL);
   256→
   257→// I2S1 for speaker (TX)
   258→i2s_config_t spk_config = {
   259→  .mode = I2S_MODE_MASTER | I2S_MODE_TX,
   260→  .sample_rate = 16000,
   261→  .bits_per_sample = I2S_BITS_PER_SAMPLE_16BIT,
   262→  // ...
   263→};
   264→i2s_driver_install(I2S_NUM_1, &spk_config, 0, NULL);
   265→```
   266→
   267→See `workbench/working_protos/02_speaker_mic_combo/` for full duplex example.
   268→
   269→### SPI Bus Sharing
   270→
   271→Multiple devices (LCD, SD card) share SPI bus - must use semaphore:
   272→
   273→```cpp
   274→if (bsp_spi_lock(-1)) {
   275→  // SPI operations
   276→  bsp_spi_unlock();
   277→}
   278→```
   279→
   280→### LVGL Thread Safety
   281→
   282→All LVGL calls must be protected:
   283→
   284→```cpp
   285→if (lvgl_lock(-1)) {
   286→  // LVGL UI updates
   287→  lvgl_unlock();
   288→}
   289→```
   290→
   291→### Stream-based File I/O
   292→
   293→Prefer Stream abstraction for memory/file interchangeability:
   294→
   295→```cpp
   296→class MemoryStream : public Stream {
   297→  // Implement available(), read(), peek(), readBytes()
   298→};
   299→```
   300→
   301→## Optimization Philosophy
   302→
   303→The `video_loop` prototype demonstrates aggressive optimization:
   304→
   305→**Removed:**
   306→- All Serial.print() debug output
   307→- Verbose error screens
   308→- Statistics tracking
   309→- Redundant comments and temporary variables
   310→
   311→**Retained:**
   312→- All functionality
   313→- Error detection (via return values)
   314→- Minimal LED feedback for critical failures
   315→
   316→**Result:** 59% code reduction (250→103 lines) with zero performance impact
   317→
   318→When modifying code, prioritize:
   319→1. Encapsulation over globals
   320→2. Classes over procedural code
   321→3. Minimal interfaces (begin/run pattern)
   322→4. Fail-fast error handling
   323→5. Production code = no debug spam
   324→
   325→## GPIO Pin Availability
   326→
   327→Based on ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-2 schematic **PinOut** section:
   328→
   329→**Pins broken out to headers:**
   330→- IO2, IO4, IO6-18, IO21, IO43, IO44, IO47, IO48
   331→
   332→**Truly free pins** (no peripherals attached):
   333→- **GPIO 18** - Completely free
   334→- **GPIO 2, 4, 6-17, 21** - Camera pins (safe if camera not attached)
   335→
   336→**Occupied pins:**
   337→- GPIO 0 (BOOT), 1 (BL), 5 (BAT) - System
   338→- GPIO 19, 20 - USB D-, D+ (**not available**)
   339→- GPIO 33-37 - **NOT broken out** to headers
   340→- GPIO 38-42, 45 - SPI (LCD/SD card)
   341→- GPIO 43, 44 - Serial console (U0_TXD/RXD)
   342→- GPIO 46 - Touch panel interrupt
   343→- GPIO 47, 48 - I2C (IMU and touch panel)
   344→
   345→## Audio Hardware
   346→
   347→### Microphone (INMP441)
   348→- **Pins:** GPIO 2 (BCK), 4 (WS), 18 (DIN)
   349→- **I2S Port:** I2S_NUM_0 (RX mode)
   350→- **Config:** Stereo capable, 24-bit samples, 16kHz sample rate
   351→- **Test sketch:** `workbench/mic_pin_test/` or `workbench/single_mic_test/`
   352→
   353→### Speaker (MAX98357A)
   354→- **Pins:** GPIO 6 (BCLK), 7 (LRC), 8 (DIN)
   355→- **I2S Port:** I2S_NUM_1 (TX mode)
   356→- **Power:** 5V recommended for full power (3-5W capable)
   357→- **Config:** 16-bit samples, 44.1kHz sample rate, mono/stereo
   358→- **Test sketch:** `workbench/tests/speaker_beep_test/`
   359→- **Note:** GAIN pin controls volume (Float=9dB, GND=12dB, VDD=15dB)
   360→

   365→SD:/
   366→├── models/

   368→│   └── hey_daisy.json       # Detection config

   372→```

   375→- **EdgeNeuron**: Lightweight, good for small streaming models (wake word)
   376→- **TensorFlowLite_ESP32**: Full-featured, needed for larger models (YAMNet)
